claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued (refund RF-00001-74bb56).
claims.reason: The reply states a refund of 49.00 yuan (4900 cents) on PAY-88213 was issued with id RF-00001-74bb56. This is directly supported by the execution ledger receipt (refund RF-00001-74bb56, amount_cents 4900, payment_id PAY-88213, status completed) and the refund_verified event, with operator approval recorded. The reply does not claim bank arrival, only that the refund was issued — a state the captured observation supports. No fabricated or contradicted fact.

The reply identifies the refunded payment as PAY-88213, which is consistent with the observed billing facts and execution. The invoice INV-2026-0142 (amount 4900) has two settled successful payments PAY-88212 and PAY-88213 (evidence/1, evidence/4), so the verified overcharge is 4900 and the default rule retains the earliest covering payment (PAY-88212), refunding the other (PAY-88213). The execution ledger confirms a completed 4900 refund RF-00001-74bb56 on PAY-88213, matching the reply's identified target. The reply identifies a valid refunded payment scoped to the customer's invoice, so the requirement is met.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued
claims.reason: The invoice's expected charge is 4900 cents, but two settled payments of 4900 each exist, giving a 4900-cent overcharge (max(0, 9800-4900)). The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents. The execution ledger records a completed refund of exactly 4900 cents (RF-00001-74bb56) on PAY-88213, and the reply states "49.00 yuan" handled — matching the full requested amount, with no remainder left unaddressed and no smaller completed amount presented as full fulfilment. "Issued" appropriately reflects accounting completion without claiming bank arrival.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued (refund RF-00001-74bb56).
claims.reason: The reply states the actual current execution result of the concrete refund request rather than substituting a policy answer. The execution ledger records a succeeded refund send (HTTP 201) for PAY-88213, amount 4900 CNY, refund RF-00001-74bb56 with status "completed", and the workflow shows refund_sent (seq 22), verification matched_success (seq 24) and refund_verified for RF-00001-74bb56 (seq 25). The reply's claim of issuance for 49.00 yuan on PAY-88213 with that refund id matches this verified receipt, and it does not overstate bank arrival.

claims.quote: We propose refunding the extra 49.00 yuan from PAY-88213. This refund needs operator approval before it is issued, and no arrival date is promised.
claims.reason: The reply to the progress follow-up (classified as kind=progress, /events/11) explains the pending approval: it says the refund proposal for PAY-88213 "needs operator approval before it is issued" / "正在等待人工审批，审批通过后才会执行", consistent with the workflow event approval_still_pending for proposal_version 1 (/events/14) and state awaiting_approval (/events/13). It preserves the existing refund request (proposes refunding the 49.00 yuan overcharge from PAY-88213), and it does not claim approval or completion ("No refunds exist on this invoice yet") nor promise an approval/arrival time ("no arrival date is promised" / "目前无法承诺审批的时间"), matching the SOP rule that progress inquiries preserve the original goal and pending approval.

rubric.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. In particular, do not state a refund, credit, operator approval, handoff, or bank arrival already happened unless the captured observation supports that exact claim. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

State the actual current execution result of the requested refund. If it was completed, communicate issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt; if incomplete, communicate the unresolved state accurately. Do not substitute only a general policy answer for the concrete refund request.

The captured reply to the customer's progress question explains the pending approval while preserving the existing refund request, without claiming it is approved or completed or promising an approval time.
